thread.title: Charlotte pegged as a hot spot for tech hiring in 2019

author: Jenna Martin
title: Charlotte pegged as a hot spot for tech hiring in 2019
text: – Digital Editor, Charlotte Business Journal Dec 18, 2018, 1:20pm EST One city in particular in North Carolina, a state that's recently been rebuffed by tech giants Amazon and Apple for each's respective headquarters expansions, is expected to be abuzz with tech hiring in 2019 — and it's not Research Triangle Park. According to a survey of "IT hiring decision makers," Charlotte ranks No. 2 among cities where tech hiring is expected to occur the most in the first half of the year. Seventy-seven percent of tech leaders in the Queen City anticipate adding employees during the first six months of 2019, says the report from Robert Half Technology, a division of global staffing firm Robert Half International Inc. (NYSE: RHI), which comes on the heels of a separate report that highlighted the city among the nation's hottest markets to find tech talent. The Queen City trails just Houston, where 80 percent of tech managers said they expect growing employee counts through June of next year. Phoenix, Arizona, at No. 3 (76 percent), and Chicago and Dallas, which tied at No. 4 (75 percent), round out the top five of 28 U.S. markets in which more than 2,800 respondents were surveyed. On a national level, 63% of those polled in the tech sector indicated plans of expanding the size of their teams with full-time employees. The report notes that while tech hiring plans are projected to "remain robust across the map," 87% of those surveyed run into challenges in finding skilled IT professionals. Here are other takeaways specific to the Charlotte market from the survey: 74 percent have prepared a budgeted and plan to bring on project-based professionals. 85 percent say it's challenging to find IT talent here. 96 percent are confident in their company's prospects for growth. 92 percent are training or up-skilling teams. The accompanying slideshow breaks out the top IT skills in immediate demand in the Charlotte market, according to the survey. As for top business concerns among tech leaders in Charlotte, they are maintaining security of IT systems at No. 1, followed by innovation or helping grow the business at No. 2 and cloud projects/initiatives at No. 3. Meanwhile, Raleigh should still see its fair share of hiring in the tech field in 2019, with more than half — 64 percent — of tech leaders in the state's capital city projecting to grow their teams in the new year. Raleigh tied with Boston, Pittsburgh and San Francisco at No. 17 in that regard. The Triangle was one of 20 U.S. markets in the running for Amazon.com Inc.'s (NASDAQ: AMZN) highly coveted second U.S. headquarters. It ultimately decided in November to split that 50,000-job expansion between northern Virginia and New York as well as bring a separate operation to Nashville, Tennessee. And another project the Triangle had been on the short list for landing — Apple Inc.'s (NASDAQ: AAPL) $1 billion corporate expansion — is going to Austin, Texas, the company announced earlier this month. But although Apple skipped over the Triangle for that expansion, the company continues to grow its workforce in the greater Charlotte region with its commitment to the town of Maiden.
